claims.text: Coinsurance is a percentage share of a covered service's allowed amount; official definition quoted verbatim
claims.quote: The percentage of costs of a covered health care service you pay (20%, for example) after you've paid your deductible.

claims.text: Office visit example: $100 allowed amount, 20% coinsurance; after the deductible you pay $20 and the plan pays the rest ($80)
claims.quote: for an office visit is $100 and your coinsurance is 20%. If you've paid your deductible: You pay 20% of $100, or $20. The insurance company pays the rest.

claims.text: If the deductible is not met you pay the full $100; FAQ: before the deductible is met you pay the full allowed amount
claims.quote: If you haven't met your deductible: You pay the full allowed amount, $100.

claims.text: Full-year example: $12,000 covered costs, $3,000 deductible, 20% coinsurance; you pay $1,800 of the remaining $9,000, total $4,800 (plan pays the other $7,200 by arithmetic)
claims.quote: Allowable costs are $12,000. Deductible: $3,000 Coinsurance: 20% You'd pay all of the first $3,000 (your deductible). You'll pay 20% of the remaining $9,000, or $1,800 (your coinsurance).

claims.text: Total for the year is $4,800; once the out-of-pocket maximum is reached the plan pays for covered services
claims.quote: So your total out-of-pocket costs would be $4,800

claims.text: FAQ answers: coinsurance applies after the deductible; with 20% coinsurance you pay 20% and the plan pays 80%
claims.quote: The percentage of costs of a covered health care service you pay (20%, for example) after you've paid your deductible.

claims.text: Table: deductible is what you pay for covered services before the plan starts paying (example $2,000)
claims.quote: The amount you pay for covered health care services before your insurance plan starts to pay. With a $2,000 deductible, for example, you pay the first $2,000 of covered services yourself.

claims.text: Table: copay is a fixed dollar amount ($30 example); coinsurance is a percentage (20% example)
claims.quote: A fixed amount you pay for a plan-covered service, like $30. ... A percentage of the cost that you pay for each plan-covered service, like 20%.

claims.text: Table: premium is the monthly amount you pay to keep coverage whether or not you use care
claims.quote: A monthly amount you pay for coverage whether you get services or not.

claims.text: FAQ (rewritten): many plans pay for certain services, like a checkup, before the deductible is met; after the deductible you usually pay a copay or coinsurance
claims.quote: After you pay your deductible, you usually pay only a copayment or coinsurance for covered services. ... Many plans pay for certain services, like a checkup or disease management programs, before you've met your deductible.

claims.text: Preventive care is often covered at 100% before the deductible
claims.quote: All Marketplace health plans pay the full cost of certain preventive benefits even before you meet your deductible.
